title: Differentially Private Eigenspectrum Monitor Logs for Hallucination Detection

contributions.purpose: Establish whether differential privacy can protect eigenspectrum-based hallucination monitor logs while preserving utility.
contributions.mechanism: First evaluation of DP for eigenspectrum-based hallucination detection using a pre-registered privacy-utility tradeoff framework with explicit decision criteria.
contributions.evaluation: Pre-registered viability threshold (5-point AUROC drop) framework applied at epsilon=5, delta=10^-5.
contributions.domain: differential privacy for LLM hallucination monitoring
contributions.source_quote: We provide the first evaluation of differential privacy for eigenspectrum-based hallucination detection, establishing a rigorous privacy-utility tradeoff framework with pre-registered decision criteria.

contributions.purpose: Reduce the noise cost of DP on high-dimensional hidden-state queries.
contributions.mechanism: Apply the Rank-1 Singular Multivariate Gaussian (R1SMG) mechanism, exploiting DP-proof geometry for dimension-independent noise scaling versus standard isotropic Gaussian.
contributions.evaluation: R1SMG achieves 360x lower noise than Gaussian at epsilon=5, delta=10^-5, yielding 4.4 higher AUROC points (0.536 vs 0.492).
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that R1SMG achieves 360x lower noise than the Gaussian mechanism at identical privacy budget, yielding 4.4 AUROC points higher utility.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the inherent privacy provided by eigenspectrum dimensionality reduction alone.
contributions.mechanism: Run canary-ID membership attacks against compressed eigenspectrum (40,960-dim hidden states to K=10 eigenvalues) without any DP noise.
contributions.evaluation: Even without DP noise, canary-ID attackers remain at chance level, indicating compression itself destroys identifying information.
contributions.source_quote: We discover that eigenspectrum compression provides substantial inherent privacy: even without DP noise, canary-ID attackers remain at chance level.

contributions.purpose: Assess practical viability of DP-protected eigenspectrum monitoring.
contributions.mechanism: Compare best DP mechanism (R1SMG) utility against the clip-only baseline under the pre-registered threshold.
contributions.evaluation: Negative result: R1SMG incurs a 13.5-point AUROC drop from the clip-only baseline (0.672), far exceeding the 5-point viability threshold.
contributions.domain: differential privacy for LLM hallucination monitoring
contributions.source_quote: We conclude with a negative result: despite R1SMG's dramatic noise reduction, DP-protected eigenspectrum monitoring incurs unacceptable utility loss (13.5-point AUROC drop) at tested privacy budgets.

self_declared_provenance.quote: the Rank-1 Singular Multivariate Gaussian (R1SMG) mechanism (Ji & Li, 2023) achieves dimension-independent noise scaling by exploiting the geometry of DP proofs, offering a potential path to practical privacy protection.

INSIDE (Chen et al., 2024) demonstrates that eigenspectrum analysis of hidden state covariance matrices provides effective hallucination detection, motivating our investigation of privacy-preserving variants.
Our work investigates whether the rank-1 structure of eigenspectrum changes enables more efficient noise calibration.
Our work differs by focusing specifically on monitoring systems that log eigenspectrum statistics rather than protecting inference itself.

notes: NEGATIVE-RESULT paper: both DP mechanisms fail the pre-registered viability threshold; R1SMG's 360x noise reduction still yields a 13.5-point AUROC drop. Notably reports an inherent-privacy finding (attackers at chance without DP), weakening the assumed threat model. Adapts existing R1SMG mechanism (Ji & Li 2023) and INSIDE/EigenScore detection (Chen et al. 2024) rather than proposing new detector.
